title: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum

constraints.meaning: At least one number, at most 100.
constraints.impact: Brute force (try startValue = 1, 2, 3, … and walk nums for each) passes here. One pass with a running sum is O(n) and shows the prefix-sum idea.

constraints.meaning: Values can be negative, zero or positive.
constraints.impact: A running sum stays within 100 · 100 = 10⁴ in absolute value, so int is enough. Only negative values can push the step-by-step sum down.
When the sum never goes down (LC 2: [1,2]), the answer is still 1, not 0 or less.

bruteForce.summary: try startValue = 1, 2, 3, … For each one, walk nums and add the numbers; stop at the first startValue whose step-by-step sum never drops below 1. The answer can be up to 1 + 100 · 100, so this is O(n · answer). It forgets everything it learned about nums each time it tries the next startValue.
